title: The Sounds of Music: Notes, Rhythm and Raga
summary: Pitch, beat and the seven notes in both Western and Indian music.

steps.title: Music is organised sound
sentences: Music is made of sounds arranged in time.
The three main parts are pitch, how high or low a note is, rhythm, the pattern of beats, and tempo, how fast or slow it is.
Singing, clapping and drumming all use them.

steps.title: Seven notes
sentences: Western music names its notes A B C D E F G.
Indian classical music uses seven basic notes: sa, ri, ga, ma, pa, dha and ni.
In Carnatic music these are called swaras.
points: Sa ri ga ma pa dha ni

steps.title: Raga and tala
sentences: A raga is a set of notes and rules for how to use them, and it creates a special mood.
A tala is the cycle of beats that keeps time, such as adi tala with eight beats.
Together they allow musicians to improvise and still stay in order.

steps.title: Instruments
sentences: The veena, violin and flute carry the melody, and the mridangam and tabla keep the rhythm.
Instruments are grouped as strings, winds, percussion and keyboards.
Trying any instrument, even a simple drum, trains your ears and your patience.

facts: Tamil Nadu has a very old musical tradition, and the Chennai Music Season in December is one of the largest classical music festivals in the world.
The tabla and the mridangam are both drums, but they come from different traditions.
A metronome is a device that clicks a steady beat.

quiz.q: How many basic notes does Indian classical music use?
quiz.why: Sa, ri, ga, ma, pa, dha, ni.
